08-rules/items/crystal-of-naphkon.html.title: Crystal of Naphkon
08-rules/items/crystal-of-naphkon.html.description:
Turn this on to show this item in the Shared Library.
The Crystal of Naphkon can be used to home in on the kidnapped psyches of Brendan Sterling and the others. It requires a large amethyst to fashion, then a psychic or POW-based activation roll to receive the vision.To fashion a crystal of Naphkon requires a large amethyst, which can be easily purchased in New York City for $20 for a rough, poor quality stone. Higher quality stones cost $50 to $100+.See Create Crystal of Naphkon, page 161.Once created, the crystal may be used to home in on the kidnapped psyches.A character may activate the crystal with either:
A successful Clairvoyance roll and 1D6+1 magic points, or
A successful Psychometry roll and 1D6+1 magic points if touching a possession of one of the victims, such as bedding or an empty bottle from the cellar.
Without psychic talents, activation requires:
A successful Hard POW roll, and
1D8+5 magic points.
The process is similar to viewing different times and places, but the costs and process are slightly different due to the psychic turmoil caused by this event.The vision reveals six men and women trapped in an unfurnished room with marble floors and walls. All of them are wearing amethyst necklaces. They are dressed in loose tunics, and the men have forked beards.One is frantically pounding on the door, while others pace or slump dejectedly. There is one tall, thin window, too narrow to squeeze through.Suddenly, all of the inhabitants react, apparently to sounds outside. One of them runs to the window and looks down. The viewer now sees that they are in a high tower.Down below, flames are spreading through a partly ruined city, and tunic-clad, gray-eyed people are fighting shaggy umber-colored humanoids. A six-legged, white-furred beast with a horn jutting from its head rampages past.The vision ends abruptly with a sense of impending doom for the victims.The experience costs the viewer 0/1D4 Sanity points.Heroes who wish to rescue Brendan Sterling and the others need to figure out how to get to them and gather their psyches. See Chapter 6 for details on how this rescue can be accomplished.The heroes can attempt this rescue practically any time, though it is best accomplished before tracking down the Lomarian-possessed bodies.Having experienced the vision of Sterling and the others, a hero may attempt a Cthulhu Mythos roll to deduce their location in ancient Lomar.Alternatively, heroes using the details from the vision may conduct research in any Mythos tomes they encounter or possess to fathom the victims' location. Use the tome in question's Mythos Rating to determine if the heroes find matching information concerning:
Gray-eyed peoples: Lomarians
Shaggy umber-colored humanoids: Voormi
Six-legged furred beasts: Gnoph-kehs
Together, these details place Brendan Sterling and the others in forgotten Lomar, some 25,000 years in the past.See Call of Cthulhu Rulebook, page 175 for Mythos tome ratings.The Keeper is advised to read the opening section of Chapter 6, which includes advice about keeping the mind-swapped victims' plight in the heroes' thoughts throughout the campaign.

08-rules/items/heart-of-dreams.html.title: Heart of Dreams
08-rules/items/heart-of-dreams.html.description:
Turn this on to show this item in the Shared Library.
Hearts of Dreams are rare items, much sought after by those who know and understand their abilities. The hearts are known by different names; many have cultural associations or are related to the land of dream, and much myth and folklore surround them.One legend concerning the hearts seems to cross cultural boundaries and concerns the foul keepers or guardians of the hearts, who torment those who risk using a heart’s power without due deference to Hypnos, Lord of Dream.These strange devices usually take the form of a red crystalline cube run through with jagged lines of yellow material.A Heart of Dreams is used to view other places in dream. These places could include distant lands, planets, and other dimensions.In addition, a heart can enable its user to physically bring items or living things back with them from the Dreamlands, provided such things are held by the dreamer.Using a Heart of Dreams requires a successful Cthulhu Mythos roll.In addition, a successful Luck roll determines whether the heart’s keeper detects the item’s use.The Luck roll may be ignored if an Extreme success is achieved with the Cthulhu Mythos roll, indicating that the user did not displease Hypnos, the prime creator and owner of the hearts.
